id: suite:escrow-split:tests/public/escrow.test.ts :: [boundary-2] a pro bono task records no releases across both gates and redelivery
name: a pro bono task records no releases across both gates and redelivery
message: the hidden tests have not passed
reason: For bounty 0, the spec says “no release is ever recorded,” so the hidden-test share remains unreleased. When UAT arrives with “the hidden-test share has not been released,” the spec requires that “it fails with an error saying the hidden tests have not passed,” contrary to the test’s expected success.

id: suite:escrow-split:tests/public/escrow.test.ts :: [boundary-2] pro bono status also holds at both share endpoints
name: pro bono status also holds at both share endpoints
message: the hidden tests have not passed
reason: For a zero bounty, the spec says "no release is ever recorded." Its UAT rule says that when "the hidden-test share has not been released," handling "fails with an error"; remaining "pro bono" does not require the successful UAT return asserted by the test.

id: suite:gherkin-parse:tests/public/valid-features.test.ts :: [happy-1] handles CRLF, mixed leading whitespace and no final newline
name: handles CRLF, mixed leading whitespace and no final newline
message:
Expected values to be strictly deep-equal:
+ actual - expected

...
          table: null,
+         text: ' an account'
-         text: ' an account  '
        },
        {
          docString: null,

reason: The spec requires each step’s "text after the keyword and one space", which includes the remaining leading space and both trailing spaces in "Given  an account  ". The implementation trims the trailing spaces; the mixed indentation and extra whitespace make this an uncommon but plausible input.

id: suite:gherkin-parse:tests/private/parse-errors.test.ts :: [unhappy-1] rejects step-like lines without the required space after the keyword
name: rejects step-like lines without the required space after the keyword
reason: The spec defines step text as coming after "the keyword and one space" and requires that "a line inside a scenario that is none of the forms above, fails at that line." These malformed separators therefore require a ParseError at line 3; a tab separator is an uncommon but plausible formatting mistake.

id: suite:licence-scan:tests/private/licence-expressions.test.ts :: [unhappy-2] singleton legacy arrays are not automatically treated as permissive
name: singleton legacy arrays are not automatically treated as permissive
message:
Expected values to be strictly equal:

true !== false
reason: The spec says an old-style "licenses" array is read as "each entry's 'type' joined by OR", so a singleton preserves its licence's verdict. It explicitly makes "GPLv3" copyleft, "UNLICENSED" and expressions that do not parse unknown, and "any identifier starting 'LGPL'" permitted; the implementation incorrectly permits the singleton UNLICENSED array.

id: suite:licence-scan:tests/private/licence-expressions.test.ts :: [unhappy-2] a parser must consume trailing input even after a permitted OR branch
name: a parser must consume trailing input even after a permitted OR branch
reason: The spec says "Licences are read as SPDX expressions" and an "expression that does not parse" fails as "unknown"; malformed syntax such as the semicolon in "MIT OR ISC;" therefore requires failure despite the permitted MIT branch. The test deliberately supplies malformed expressions to probe parser validation.

id: suite:patch-apply:tests/public/apply-patch.test.ts :: [happy-4] rejects a deletion without hunks when the file is nonempty
name: rejects a deletion without hunks when the file is nonempty
message:
Expected values to be strictly equal:

true !== false
reason: The spec requires rejection with reason "no match" unless "the file is empty when it has no hunks"; this deletion has no hunks but targets a nonempty file. This is an unusual boundary case involving the explicitly described headerless deletion format.

id: suite:patch-apply:tests/public/apply-patch.test.ts :: [happy-2] measures each offset from the old start adjusted only by preceding line-count changes
name: measures each offset from the old start adjusted only by preceding line-count changes
message:
Expected values to be strictly deep-equal:
+ actual - expected
... Skipped lines

  [
    {
      hunk: 1,
      offset: 1,
      path: 'a.ts'
...
      hunk: 2,
+     offset: 0,
-     offset: -1,
      path: 'a.ts'
    }
  ]
reason: The spec says a hunk's stated line is its "old start line moved by the lines the hunks before it added or removed," and its offset is measured from that line. The first hunk adds one net line, so the second hunk's adjusted stated line is 6; D matches at line 5, requiring offset -1.

id: suite:reverse-diff:tests/private/unmapped.test.ts :: [unhappy-1] discovers paths from standalone old and new headers in their textual order
name: discovers paths from standalone old and new headers in their textual order
message:
Expected values to be strictly deep-equal:
+ actual - expected

  {
    diff: '--- a/docs/z.md\n' +
      '+++ b/docs/a.md\n' +
      '@@ -1 +1 @@\n' +
      '-old\n' +
      '+new\n' +
      '--- a/docs/a.md\n' +
+     '+++ b/view/mapped.ts\n' +
-     '+++ b/src/mapped.ts\n' +
      '@@ -1 +1 @@\n' +
      '-old\n' +
      '+new\n',
    unmapped: [
      'docs/z.md',
reason: The spec says a directory entry “maps every path under it” and “unmapped paths are reported in the order they first appear,” requiring view/mapped.ts to become src/mapped.ts and the reported paths to be deduplicated in textual order. This valid multi-file unified diff without diff --git separators is an uncommon but plausible input; the spec does not require those separators.

id: suite:tool-versions:tests/public/reporting.test.ts :: [boundary-3] all differing later versions are grouped in one conflict per tool
name: all differing later versions are grouped in one conflict per tool
message:
Expected values to be strictly equal:

2 !== 3
reason: The spec says Go comes from “the toolchain line of go.mod, then its go line” and “the first source wins and a disagreement is reported.” Both directives contain differing exact versions, so Go must also have a conflict; these are ordinary repository declarations like the spec’s examples.

id: suite:tool-versions:tests/private/reporting.test.ts :: [boundary-3] every exact loser is reported with all sources present in reverse priority order
name: every exact loser is reported with all sources present in reverse priority order
reason: The spec says “Go comes from the toolchain line of go.mod, then its go line” and “The first source wins and a disagreement is reported,” requiring the differing Go versions to appear as a conflict too. Multiple conflicting declarations across every tool are an uncommon but plausible combination.

id: suite:tool-versions:tests/public/parsing.test.ts :: [unhappy-1] no exact version is extracted from aliases ranges or malformed versions
name: no exact version is extracted from aliases ranges or malformed versions
reason: The spec says “anything else is not a version” and “no version is guessed, rounded or taken from part of a range.” Thus “22 || 20” must be skipped; extracting “22” from the Go directive violates that requirement.
